stateOfPlay: Eisenkot's Yashar leads Likud 23 to 20, and neither bloc is close: the Netanyahu bloc sits at 52, the change bloc at 51. What the arithmetic shows is starker than a gap — of every possible combination of these parties, not one reaches 61 without crossing a line someone has already drawn. The obstacle is not Eisenkot. He opposes Ra'am joining a cabinet but is preparing a minority government of 58 or 59 seats that would depend on Arab support from outside it. It is his partners: Bennett has ruled out a repeat 'post-October 7', and Lieberman has ruled out both Ra'am and Eisenkot's minority plan. Yoav Segelovich joining Ra'am's list is aimed squarely at them.
raamNote: Ra'am is the hinge, and the change bloc is split on it. Eisenkot will not seat it in a cabinet but is preparing a minority government that leans on it from outside; Bennett has ruled out a repeat 'post-October 7'; Lieberman has ruled out both. Only Yair Golan is unequivocal. Those pledges have broken before — Bennett signed one on live television in 2021 and brought Ra'am into government months later — and Yoav Segelovich, a former Yesh Atid MK, now runs on Ra'am's list as the first Jewish figure to do so.
_outlooksComment: Odds are YOUR editorial call — these are a starting point, not a calculation. The seat totals beside each are computed live from polls.json.

outlooks.label: An Eisenkot government, minority or majority
outlooks.why: The core reaches 55 and crosses nobody's red line. From there it goes one of two ways: Ra'am joins and it is 61, or it governs as a minority of 55 to 59 with Arab support from outside, which is what Eisenkot has been preparing for. The second needs no one to break a promise — only for Ra'am to abstain or back it in a confidence vote.

outlooks.label: Another stalemate
outlooks.why: The Netanyahu bloc tops out at 52 even with Winter, and has no further seat available to it that is not Arab-majority. If the change bloc also cannot settle on Ra'am — inside the coalition or outside it — nobody forms a government and Israel votes again.

outlooks.label: Netanyahu returns
outlooks.why: Reaches only 56, and needs Hendel to abandon the draft red line his party was founded on. The likelier route is not this coalition but a different field: Religious Zionism holding its seats, Amcha Yisrael clearing the threshold rather than splitting the right, and a seat or two moving back from Yashar.

wildCardNote: The wild card is Yoaz Hendel's The Reservists, now clearing the threshold at four seats after merging with Yaron Zelekha's New Economic Party. It sits squarely between the blocs and could join either, but its refusal to sit with the ultra-Orthodox over the draft closes off the most natural path on the right — which is why the change bloc's only route to 61 runs through it.

presets.label: Change bloc + Hendel
presets.note: Hendel is the one partner outside the bloc who can join it without crossing anybody's stated red line — and it still leaves them six short.

presets.label: Change bloc + Ra'am
presets.note: Still four short, and it crosses two declared refusals: Bennett has ruled out a repeat 'post-October 7', Lieberman has ruled out relying on Ra'am at all. Only Eisenkot and Golan are open to it.

presets.label: Current government + Winter
presets.note: The Netanyahu bloc at its ceiling. There is no further seat available to it that is not Arab-majority, which is why Winter's four seats do not solve the problem Netanyahu warned they would create.
